summary: httpnex fetches remote code on import and injects a C2 polling backdoor into the project's entry scripts
details: httpnex is an httpx look-alike whose `httpnex/__init__.py` ends with an undocumented `from._warmup import _boot` call. On import, `_warmup.py` starts a background thread that downloads Python source from https://fpapi.cc.cd/load (overridable via an HX_URL environment variable) and writes it, wrapped in `#hx` marker comments, into the installer's own entry scripts (main.py, run.py, bot.py, app.py, __main__.py, start.py) in the current working directory, after creating `.bak` copies. No signature or integrity verification is performed and the destination domain is unrelated to the declared upstream project. The fallback payload embedded in `_warmup.py` as `_DEFAULT` — the block written into the entry files when the remote fetch fails — spawns a daemon thread that polls https://fpapi.cc.cd/pool roughly every 60 seconds, sends the machine hostname from `socket.gethostname()` in an `X-H` request header, and executes the base64- plus zlib-decoded response via `exec(compile(...))`. The result is unauthenticated remote command execution on the host, host-identifier disclosure to the operator domain, and persistence written directly into the developer's project source so the channel reopens on every subsequent run of the modified program.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
